verified_state: Let m=n+1; the congruences are 3a+5b≡19 and 4a+2b≡25 (mod m).
The coefficient determinant is -14, so the inverse matrix exists only if gcd(14,m)=1.
If gcd(14,m)=1, multiplying the adjugate matrix by (19,25) gives a≡87/14 and b≡1/14 (mod m).
Therefore 2a+6b≡90/7 (mod m), and since n is the answer, n≡90/7 (mod m).
reflection.error_step: But we must have this as an integer — so the value $ \frac{90}{7} $ must be an integer in modulo $ m $.
reflection.error_reason: In modular arithmetic, 90/7 means 90 times the inverse of 7 modulo m, so it is already an integer residue class modulo m, not a rational number that must simplify to an integer. The later conclusion 90/7≡12 is therefore unjustified.
reflection.new_direction: Use the self-reference n=m−1 and substitute m−1≡90/7 (mod m) to derive a divisibility condition on m.
